system.summary: Numerical nomenclators provisionally grouped by 1752, 1756 and 1763; homophones and codebook ordering remain unverified.
system.notes: Underlines and carets preserved in audit/tokens.json; their cryptographic role is unknown. Failed density tests do not prove random ordering or impossibility of a ciphertext-only solution.

prior_solution.where: DECODE says other Hellen letters were solved by Lyonet; none found printed or online

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Fetched the eight DECODE transcriptions and images; parsed into code groups.
Searched Politische Correspondenz 9, 13, 22, 23 for printed or quoted text of these reports.
1763 code: gap 1555-2005, flat frequencies, clustered homophones (900-923 = ~5.7%, plausibly 'de').
One-part alphabetical code: linear mapping to PC French word list; density correlation 0.31, no readable text.
Searched DECODE for intercepted Frederick->Hellen letters and web for keys (Tomokiyo, Lyonet, de Leeuw).
Two alphabetical sections (1-1555 common words, 2005-3920 rarer words): density vs. PC word lists per section, correlations -0.25 to 0.34.
Second session (19 Sept 2026): re-searched de Leeuw (Diplomacy & Statecraft 1999) and Lyonet literature for a printed Hellen key or decipherment; none found online.
One-part test on codes A (1752, R1953) and B (1756, R1049): density vs PC word lists, corr -0.08 to 0.33; flat frequencies (max 10/841, 10/511). Both are two-part codes like C.
20 September 2026: audited parser; retained uncertain digits, marks and cipher adjacent to cleartext; excluded empty newline fragments and heading year. Regression checks passed.
20 September 2026: manuscript IMG_R1953_I13448_P3 confirms both instances of the near-repeated three-line block. Do not deduplicate the transcription.
20 September 2026: downgraded earlier random-code and homophone assertions; density test failures do not establish these properties.
20 September 2026: retrieved full de Leeuw thesis. Article notes identify Fagel 5177 and Boerhaave Arch 162-r; no Prussian codes solved April 1757–October 1763 is reported.
20 September 2026: official catalogue lists digitized Hellen decipherments 1752–1753 in Fagel 5206. Old scan route 404; current shell accessible; service API timeout. No parallel text read.
20 September 2026: cached DECODE catalogue identifies 23-page Prussia cipher key R2824, dated 1746, Fagel 5345. Not yet inspected or tested.
20 September 2026: full public R2824 record rejects that lead: key is for Dutch envoy Baron van Reede going to Prussia, not a Prussian chancery key. Images require authentication and were not viewed.
20 September 2026: browser confirmed Nationaal Archief viewer renders an empty catalogue area and a temporary scan-maintenance notice; no Fagel 5206 manuscript image retrieved.

outcome.method_basis: No plaintext or key was found (Politische Correspondenz and the de Leeuw/Lyonet literature were searched; R2824 was rejected); the Fagel 5206 decipherments could not be retrieved.
outcome.notes: Open; no cipher plaintext verified. Next: retrieve Fagel 5206 parallel decipherments. R2824 rejected as a Prussian key lead. Current access failure is not evidence of missing archives.
